label: Judgeable-offer conversion (started over offers that were not capped): Claude 5 of 14 (35.7 percent), Devin 10 of 11 (90.9), DSH 11 of 13 (84.6), Pi 7 of 14 (50.0), OpenCode 3 of 8 (37.5), a 55-point spread that is not a delivery gap.

Every start-policy offer in the final arm is a /create:* command (seven rows), and Claude started 2 of 8 start rows while Devin started 7 of 8 and DSH 6 of 8, giving segment-three rank 7 a measured start-side cost as well as a visibility count.

OpenCode brief content has parity with the hook over the whole measured typed corpus: 0 of 44 rows differ in top skill, command, policy or ambiguity, with or without the plugin's surfaceHint, so the missing includeCompiledRoute and compiledRouteTopOnly flags change nothing.

The one measured build left is an OpenCode delivery marker: a bounded prompt-free receipt written after observeEmittedAdvisorBlock plus an opencode branch in briefDelivered would move 24 of 24 rows from deliveryUnknown to a boolean and raise delivery coverage from 4 of 6 runtimes to 5 of 6, a measurement gain rather than a model-visible one.
Codex remains the only reader-facing absence: 0 of 24 rows received a brief because its hooks are unapproved, and no change in this lane can alter that; it stays with the operator.

Three candidates are hypotheses with no measurement and are not recommended: a more directive head for Claude's start rows, a higher OpenCode turn cap, and an ambiguous-prompt tie-break worth at most 1 of 9 probe rows.
